text:
[LSIG.2.5.1] **A query answers as of the clock, whatever the backing
stores.** The engine must answer every query as of the monotonic clock's sample
`t` ([LTIM.2.8.2]), over the samples inside the window as of `t` ([LSER.14.1]),
and must discount any sample outside that window the backing still stores.
`active_fraction`, `onset_rate`, and `integral` therefore all evaluate as of the
same instant `t` and may be combined in one rule without a freshness mismatch.
Worst-case query cost is O(K), bounded by the declared `.dsrt` capacity under
`realtime` (§[LSIG.5]).

An eviction as of `t` must remove only samples outside the window as of `t`, and
never what a backing keeps past its window: a step backing's carry
([LSER.13.14]), and the state [LSER.9.3.1] keeps after a window of silence. The
engine may evict as of the clock's current sample when it absorbs a sample, at
the pump's eviction sweep ([LSER.9.3.2]), and at a query before it answers it.
The monotonic clock does not go backward, so a sample evicted as of `t` lies
outside the window of every later query and every later capacity count
([LSER.13.14]). Where the engine evicts therefore changes no answer and no
refusal, and an eviction at a watch's query ([LDEB.7.4.1]) changes nothing a
later read observes.

tla.name: lsig_2_5_1__eviction_keeps_the_window
tla.note: EVICTION KEEPS THE WINDOW, within the scope: the model evicts at absorptions, each removing only what its own window as of the clock has left behind, so no sample a later window admits is gone -- the clause's 'an eviction as of t must remove only samples outside the window as of t', at the one place this model evicts -- and a query discounts the rest as of the clock (`lsig_2_5_1__seen`, whose teeth is `.teeth.stale` through `lser_14_1__read_sees_the_window`); an absorption that keeps only its own sample is refused (`.teeth.newest`). Eviction at the pump's sweep or at a query, which the clause also admits, is not drawn here. The query's O(K) cost and the `.dsrt` capacity are not modelled.
